newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: IBCA gives Dah Sing A minus rating.
newsitem.headline: IBCA gives Dah Sing A minus rating.

text.p: European ratings agency IBCA said on Monday it had assigned a short term rating of A2 and a long term rating of A minus to Hong Kong's Dah Sing Bank (DSB), a unit of Dah Sing Financial Holdings Ltd.
IBCA said that Dah Sing had a small overall market share of 0.5 to 1.0 percent of the loan and deposit markets at the end of 1995, although this share was higher in some niche markets.
"Since 1993, management has sought to diversify its loan book and revenue sources by building up its retail business in the form of unsecured personal lending and credit cards," IBCA said.
"This has produced strong growth, albeit it from a low base, and appears to offer favourable prospects," it said.
"DSB's ratings reflect its performance, capital strength and asset quality, which are good by international standards, although below some of its Hong Kong based peers."
IBCA said it had also assigned an individual rating of B and a legal rating of 4 to the bank.
